title: Shortest Path
task:
Compute the shortest distance from node 0 to every node in a directed graph containing only non-negative edge weights.

Input format:
- First line: N M S where N is the number of nodes (numbered 0 to N-1), M is the number of directed edges, and S is the source node.
- Next M lines: U V W, a directed edge from U to V with non-negative weight W.

Output format:
- Print the N shortest distances from S to nodes 0, 1, ..., N-1 on a single line, separated by single spaces, in node order.
- Print INF for any node unreachable from S.
- Read the graph from stdin and print only that single line: no labels, no node names, no extra text.

title: Stable Deduplication
task: Read n integers and print each distinct value once, preserving the order of its first appearance. The first line contains n; the second line contains n integers. Print one space-separated line. n is at least 1.

title: Word Length Summary
task: Read one line of whitespace-separated words. Print each distinct word and its character count in order of first appearance, one pair per line. Words contain only ASCII letters and comparison is case-sensitive.

title: Column Totals
task: Read an R by C integer matrix and print the sum of each column on one space-separated line. The first line contains R and C, followed by R rows of C integers.

title: Run Length Encoding
task: Read a non-empty string of lowercase ASCII letters and print consecutive runs as character followed by run length, separated by single spaces. Do not combine non-adjacent occurrences.

title: Balanced Brackets
task: Read one line containing only (), [], and {}. Print YES if brackets are correctly nested and every opener is closed; otherwise print NO. The empty string is valid.

title: Top K Frequencies
task: Read n integers and k. Print the k most frequent distinct values, ordered by descending frequency and then ascending numeric value. Input line one has n k and line two has n integers. It is guaranteed that k does not exceed the number of distinct values.

title: Minimum Meeting Rooms
task: Given n half-open meeting intervals [start, end), find the minimum number of rooms needed. A meeting ending at time t does not overlap one starting at t. The first line contains n, followed by n start/end pairs.

title: Bounded Coin Change
task: For each query amount, compute the minimum number of coins needed using unlimited coins of the given positive denominations. Print -1 when an amount cannot be formed. The first line has n q, the next line has n denominations, and the final line has q amounts. Amounts are between 0 and 10000.

title: Island Count
task: Count connected components of land in a rectangular grid. Each cell is 1 (land) or 0 (water); cells connect only horizontally or vertically, not diagonally. The first line is rows and columns, followed by the grid rows.

title: Prefix Sum Queries
task: Answer inclusive range-sum queries on a static integer array. Indices are 1-based. The first line contains n q, the second line contains n integers, then q pairs l r. Print one sum per query.

title: Shortest Paths with Negative Edges
task: Compute single-source shortest distances in a directed weighted graph that may contain negative edges. The graph is guaranteed to have no negative cycle reachable from the source. Input is N M S then M lines U V W. Print N distances in node order, using INF for unreachable nodes.

title: Offline Range Order Statistics
task: For each query l r k, print the k-th smallest value in the inclusive subarray from 1-based index l through r. The first line contains n q, the second line contains n integers, followed by q queries. k is 1-based and valid for every query.

title: Maximum Flow
task: Find the maximum flow from source 0 to sink N-1 in a directed graph with non-negative integer capacities. Input is N M followed by M lines U V C. Parallel edges are allowed and represent separate capacity. Print only the maximum flow value.

title: Minimum Spanning Forest
task: Find the total weight of a minimum spanning forest of an undirected weighted graph. The graph may be disconnected; isolated vertices contribute zero. Input is N M followed by M edges U V W, with vertices numbered 0 through N-1. Print only the total weight.

title: Lexicographically Smallest Topological Order
task: Given a directed acyclic graph, print the lexicographically smallest topological ordering of vertices numbered 1 through N. If multiple vertices have indegree zero, choose the smallest available vertex each time. Input is N M followed by M directed edges. Print the vertices on one line separated by spaces.
